title: One Piece: The Movie

sections.heading: A golden legend
sections.text: Luffy, Zoro, Nami, and Usopp cross paths with Tobio, a boy whose grandfather once sailed with the legendary pirate Woonan. Woonan supposedly gathered an enormous store of gold before disappearing. The crew becomes caught up in a treasure hunt when the ruthless pirate El Drago also pursues the legend, using a treasure map to reach the island where the gold is believed to be hidden.

sections.heading: The hunt for Woonan
sections.text: El Drago is interested only in wealth and uses his powerful voice-based Devil Fruit attacks to force his way forward. Tobio initially admires the glamorous idea of becoming a pirate, while his grandfather Ganzo understands the human cost behind Woonan’s story. The Straw Hats fight El Drago’s followers and follow the trail to Woonan’s final resting place. Their adventure gradually shifts from a race for riches into a story about a friendship that lasted longer than any treasure.

sections.heading: What the treasure means
sections.text: Luffy defeats El Drago. The legendary hoard is not the simple reward the treasure hunters expected: Woonan’s final message reveals his enduring connection to Ganzo and puts his pursuit of gold in perspective. Tobio sees that a pirate’s worth cannot be measured by money alone. The Straw Hats leave without the fortune they imagined, but the resolution restores the importance of loyalty, memory, and the people waiting for someone to return.

title: Clockwork Island Adventure

sections.heading: A stolen ship
sections.text: A peaceful break ends when the Going Merry is stolen. Luffy and the crew encounter the thieves Borodo and Akisu and learn that the Trump Pirates control Clockwork Island, a towering island supported by an extraordinary mechanical structure. The pirates’ captain, Bear King, has his own ambitions for power. The situation becomes personal when Nami is taken captive and Bear King decides he wants to marry her.

sections.heading: Climbing into danger
sections.text: The Straw Hats team up with the thief brothers and climb toward the enemy stronghold. Their route is filled with traps and battles against the Trump Pirates’ officers. Different crew members are captured along the way, forcing the others to keep moving rather than abandon the rescue. Beneath the colorful mechanical setting, the island’s people are suffering under Bear King’s rule. Borodo and Akisu’s connection also gives the adventure a family story alongside the ship rescue.

sections.heading: Breaking the pirates’ grip
sections.text: The crew reunites and confronts the Trump Pirates. Luffy overcomes Bear King, whose hardened body and heated attacks have made him a formidable opponent. The final conflict wrecks the mechanism supporting the pirates’ fortress and brings the island’s oppressive order crashing down. With Nami rescued and the Going Merry recovered, the Straw Hats can sail again. Akisu also gains a chance to reconnect with the family history that was taken from him.

title: Chopper’s Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals

sections.heading: An unexpected king
sections.text: The Straw Hats arrive near Crown Island, where unusual animals live and a legend foretells the arrival of a new king. Chopper becomes separated from the crew and lands among the animals. Because of the circumstances of his arrival and his ability to speak with them, they believe he is their promised ruler. A human boy named Mobambi lives with the island’s creatures and distrusts pirates because of what happened to his family.

sections.heading: A kingdom under threat
sections.text: Count Butler and his followers come to the island seeking the extraordinary power associated with its animal king. Their hunt puts the island’s inhabitants at risk. Chopper is uncomfortable being treated as royalty, but he cannot ignore creatures who need a doctor and a protector. While Luffy and the others search for him, Chopper forms a bond with Mobambi and must show that being part of a pirate crew does not make someone cruel.

sections.heading: Protecting a home
sections.text: Butler obtains a monstrous increase in power and attacks the defenders of the island. Luffy and the crew fight to stop him while Chopper helps protect his new friends. Their victory saves the animals from exploitation. Mobambi learns to judge the Straw Hats by their actions rather than by the word pirate. Chopper ultimately chooses to leave with his crew, carrying the experience of briefly being a king back into his life as their doctor.

title: Dead End Adventure

sections.heading: A dangerous race
sections.text: Short of money, the Straw Hats enter the Dead End Race, a secret and notoriously dangerous contest between pirate crews. The prize promises to solve their immediate financial problems, but the competition attracts more than ordinary adventurers. Among the strongest entrants is Gasparde, a former Marine who now commands his own pirate crew. A bounty hunter named Shuraiya follows a personal vendetta that brings him into the same race.

sections.heading: A rigged course
sections.text: The race sends the Going Merry through hazardous waters and pits the Straw Hats against rival ships. Luffy encounters Shuraiya and learns that his interest in Gasparde is rooted in a devastating attack on his family. A young stowaway also becomes part of the story. Gasparde’s supposed sporting participation hides a much crueler plan: he is willing to manipulate the course and sacrifice other crews to eliminate competition.

sections.heading: The real victory
sections.text: The action converges on Gasparde’s ship, where Luffy battles an enemy whose candy-like Devil Fruit body makes direct attacks difficult. With help and improvisation, Luffy finds a way to fight him and defeats him. Shuraiya’s family story reaches an emotional resolution when a survivor of his past is revealed. The Straw Hats emerge from the confrontation having protected people rather than simply won a race, turning a hunt for prize money into a struggle against betrayal and exploitation.

title: The Cursed Holy Sword

sections.heading: Zoro’s old friend
sections.text: The crew reaches an island connected to the legend of the Seven-Star Sword. Zoro encounters Saga, a swordsman from his childhood, while the others meet Maya, who is trying to protect the island from the weapon’s curse. Zoro’s loyalty to an old promise leads him away from his crew and makes his actions appear hostile. The central mystery is whether he has truly abandoned his friends or is trying to settle a debt they do not understand.

sections.heading: The sword’s influence
sections.text: Saga’s pursuit of strength has become entangled with the cursed blade. Its power feeds on hatred and threatens to grow during a coming red moon. Maya and her companions try to carry out a ritual to contain it, while the Straw Hats confront Saga’s followers. Luffy and Zoro approach the problem from different directions: Luffy wants his friend back with the crew, and Zoro must face the consequences of the bond he once made with Saga.

sections.heading: A promise beyond the curse
sections.text: The final battle exposes how much the sword has distorted Saga’s judgment. Zoro confronts his old friend and the weapon that has taken control of his ambitions. The crew’s efforts and Maya’s determination help prevent the curse from consuming the island. The resolution gives Saga a chance to live beyond the blade’s influence. Zoro returns to his companions, and the story treats loyalty as something stronger than obeying a promise that has been twisted into harm.

title: Baron Omatsuri and the Secret Island

sections.heading: An invitation to paradise
sections.text: The Straw Hats follow an invitation to a resort on Omatsuri Island. Its ruler, Baron Omatsuri, promises relaxation but requires visitors to complete a series of challenges first. The games initially seem absurd and entertaining. As the trials continue, however, the crew begins to quarrel, and the island’s cheerful atmosphere grows unsettling. Luffy is slower than some of his companions to recognize that the holiday has become a trap.

sections.heading: The island’s secret
sections.text: Crew members disappear as the challenges pull the Straw Hats apart. Luffy meets people who know there is something terribly wrong with the resort. The Baron’s strange flower, Lily Carnation, is central to the deception. The island’s hospitality conceals a system that consumes visiting pirates, while the Baron clings to the appearance of companions he lost long ago. His grief has become a reason to destroy the bonds of other crews.

sections.heading: Refusing to lose the crew
sections.text: The final confrontation becomes a desperate rescue rather than a sporting contest. Luffy learns the truth about the Baron and Lily Carnation and struggles to save his friends after being driven close to defeat. Help from other survivors gives him the chance to strike back. He destroys the force sustaining the island’s horror and frees his crew. The film ends by reaffirming the living friendships the Baron could no longer accept, and its darker imagery makes it very different in tone from a lighthearted beach adventure.

title: The Giant Mechanical Soldier of Karakuri Castle

sections.heading: A treasure inside a treasure chest
sections.text: After a storm, the Straw Hats discover an elderly woman named Roba hidden inside a treasure chest. She promises them information about a legendary golden crown if they take her home to Mecha Island. The island is filled with elaborate inventions and ruled by her son Ratchet, whose mechanical creations make even a simple visit dangerous. Nami is drawn by the treasure, while Luffy is delighted by the machines.

sections.heading: Following the island’s riddle
sections.text: The crew works through a traditional song that appears to encode the treasure’s location. Ratchet joins the search, but his interest is not limited to finding something valuable. The clues reveal that the island itself is part of a much larger living mystery. As the Straw Hats unravel the puzzle, they realize that Ratchet hopes to use that discovery to gain a weapon powerful enough to support his ambitions beyond the island.

sections.heading: A machine against a living island
sections.text: The apparent island is revealed to be an enormous turtle. Ratchet tries to control it with his machinery rather than respect it as a living creature. The Straw Hats oppose his plan, and Luffy fights Ratchet’s giant mechanical soldier. Their victory stops the scheme and allows the creature’s natural life to continue. The golden-crown legend turns out to mean something different from the straightforward pile of treasure the crew expected, closing the adventure with another reminder that the sea’s wonders resist ownership.

title: Episode of Alabasta: The Desert Princess and the Pirates

sections.heading: A kingdom on the brink
sections.text: This film retells the Alabasta conflict in a shortened theatrical form. Princess Vivi returns with the Straw Hats to a desert kingdom being torn apart by drought, suspicion, and rebellion. Crocodile, publicly seen as a protector, has secretly used Baroque Works to undermine the monarchy. Vivi’s goal is to stop her people from killing one another before the conflict becomes impossible to reverse.

sections.heading: The battle for Alabasta
sections.text: The Straw Hats split up to confront Baroque Works while Vivi races to reach the armies. Luffy faces Crocodile, whose sand powers make him especially dangerous in the desert. Early defeats force Luffy to understand the limits of his opponent’s ability rather than rely only on determination. Meanwhile, a bomb threatens the capital, raising the stakes beyond a duel between pirates. The supporting battles give the crew their own roles in protecting the country.

sections.heading: Rain and a silent farewell
sections.text: Luffy defeats Crocodile, exposing the conspiracy that drove the kingdom toward civil war. The danger in the capital is overcome, and rain becomes a symbol of the country’s chance to recover. Vivi must choose between continuing the voyage and staying with her people. She remains in Alabasta. Because openly acknowledging their friendship could endanger her position, the Straw Hats give her a silent farewell by raising the marks on their arms. The film condenses the anime arc and omits many of its smaller journeys.

title: Episode of Chopper Plus: Bloom in Winter, Miracle Sakura

sections.heading: A familiar story, changed
sections.text: This is an alternate retelling of Chopper’s introduction rather than a scene-for-scene continuation of the anime. Later crew members and the Thousand Sunny are present in a version of the Drum Island story. Nami becomes dangerously ill, and Luffy urgently searches for medical help on a winter island. The situation brings the crew into contact with Doctor Kureha and her unusual assistant, the reindeer doctor Tony Tony Chopper.

sections.heading: The doctor who believed in him
sections.text: Chopper’s history explains why he fears rejection. His appearance and abilities kept him apart from both humans and reindeer until Doctor Hiriluk treated him with kindness. Hiriluk’s dream of healing the island becomes the emotional center of the film. Wapol’s return threatens the fragile safety of the country, with new material involving his brother Musshuru distinguishing this adaptation from the original arc. Chopper has to decide whether to remain hidden or fight for the people who need him.

sections.heading: Blossoms in the snow
sections.text: Luffy confronts the returning tyrants while Chopper helps defend the island and its future. The culmination brings Hiriluk’s dream into view through the image of cherry blossoms blooming against the winter sky. Chopper accepts that he can belong to a family without giving up his identity as a doctor. He leaves with the Straw Hats. Because the film deliberately mixes later crew history into an earlier story, it should not be used as an exact episode-by-episode account of Drum Island.

title: Strong World

sections.heading: A threat to East Blue
sections.text: The Straw Hats encounter Shiki, a legendary pirate whose Devil Fruit power lets him float objects and entire islands. Shiki plans an attack that threatens East Blue, the home sea of several crew members. After recognizing Nami’s extraordinary skill at predicting weather, he abducts her and scatters her friends across floating islands filled with dangerous, altered animals. What begins as an astonishing aerial encounter becomes a rescue mission.

sections.heading: Nami’s bargain
sections.text: Nami discovers the scale of Shiki’s plan and the suffering it causes the people living under his control. She tries to protect her friends and her home through a bargain, leaving a message that the crew initially hears as a rejection. The Straw Hats fight through the islands and reunite, refusing to accept that she has willingly abandoned them. Their response turns the rescue into a direct challenge to Shiki’s gathered forces.

sections.heading: A storm above the sea
sections.text: Dressed for a raid, the crew attacks Shiki’s base. Nami’s understanding of weather becomes essential to defeating a man who controls the battlefield from the air. Luffy confronts Shiki as the floating islands and the coming storm reshape the fight. He defeats him and stops the attack on East Blue. Nami’s full message confirms the trust she placed in her friends. The ending restores the crew’s freedom to sail and contrasts Shiki’s desire to command the world with their desire to explore it.

title: Straw Hat Chase

sections.heading: The missing hat
sections.text: Luffy wakes to find that his treasured straw hat is gone. The crew joins a frantic search, and a seemingly simple theft becomes a rapid chase across ships, islands, and Marine territory. The movie is a short theatrical adventure rather than a feature-length saga, so its story focuses on one small but intensely personal objective: returning the hat that represents Luffy’s promise and identity.

sections.heading: Schneider and Buzz
sections.text: The search becomes intertwined with Schneider, an aging pirate, and his companion Buzz. Buzz is a dog with a bird transformation, which helps explain how the hat could vanish so quickly. What appears to be random mischief is connected to the relationship between the two companions. Their loyalty provides an emotional counterpoint to Luffy’s relentless determination, while the Straw Hats face the practical complications of a chase that draws the Marines’ attention.

sections.heading: A promise recovered
sections.text: The crew pushes through the obstacles and confrontations blocking Luffy’s path. He gets his hat back, and the story resolves the misunderstanding surrounding Schneider and Buzz. The adventure ends by valuing companionship over the outward appearance of strength or usefulness. It is a compact rescue-and-recovery story with a lighter tone than the larger films, built around the fact that the hat’s emotional worth is far greater than its material value.

title: Film Z

sections.heading: A rescued enemy
sections.text: The Straw Hats rescue a heavily armed man from the sea, only to discover that he is Zephyr, a former Marine admiral now known as Z. He leads the Neo Marines and intends to eradicate pirates through a plan that would also kill countless innocent people. His followers include Ain and Binz, whose abilities create immediate problems for the crew. Zephyr’s history and grief have turned his original ideals into an uncompromising campaign.

sections.heading: The End Points
sections.text: Z’s plan uses stolen Dyna Stones to destroy volcanic locations called End Points. Setting off the chain reaction would devastate the New World rather than distinguish guilty pirates from ordinary inhabitants. Luffy suffers a defeat and loses his hat to Z, making the conflict personal as well as urgent. The crew regroups, while encounters with people connected to the Marines reveal that Zephyr’s enemies do not all see him in the same way.

sections.heading: The last stand
sections.text: The Straw Hats attack to stop the final stage of the plan. Their battles with Z’s followers restore the crew and clear the way for Luffy’s rematch. Luffy defeats Z without accepting his belief that the world must be purified through indiscriminate destruction. As the Marines close in, Zephyr remains behind to face them while others escape. His final stand is tragic: the film remembers the teacher and protector he once was without treating his destructive plan as justified.

title: Film Gold

sections.heading: Welcome to Gran Tesoro
sections.text: The crew arrives at Gran Tesoro, a glittering entertainment ship ruled by Gild Tesoro. Casinos, performances, and apparent luxury promise a break from the hardships of sailing. Behind the spectacle is a system that traps visitors in debt and forces them into servitude. The Straw Hats are drawn into a rigged game, and Tesoro uses his control over gold to turn their bad luck into a threat to their freedom.

sections.heading: A heist behind the glamour
sections.text: With Zoro held as leverage, the others work on a plan to turn the casino’s own machinery against its owner. Nami reconnects with Carina, a thief from her past, whose motives are not immediately clear. The rescue becomes a heist involving disguises, timed movements, and a struggle to counter Tesoro’s ability to manipulate gold that has entered people’s bodies. The film gradually strips away the fantasy that money has made everyone aboard the ship happy.

sections.heading: Breaking the golden cage
sections.text: The plan creates an opening for the crew to escape Tesoro’s control and fight openly. Luffy confronts him as the ship becomes the stage for a spectacular gold-powered battle. Tesoro’s past explains his obsession with wealth, but it does not excuse the way he has reproduced the cruelty he once suffered. Luffy defeats him, and the people trapped by the casino gain a chance at freedom. Carina’s final maneuver provides a playful closing twist to an adventure about the difference between possessing riches and living freely.

title: Stampede

sections.heading: The Pirate Festival
sections.text: The Straw Hats attend a festival organized by Buena Festa, where pirate crews gather to hunt a treasure connected to the Pirate King. The celebration brings rivals and unlikely allies into the same arena. The contest is actually a trap built around Douglas Bullet, an immensely powerful former member of Roger’s crew. Festa intends to use the gathering to trigger a confrontation large enough to transform the balance of power at sea.

sections.heading: Bullet’s challenge
sections.text: Bullet overwhelms the competitors and uses his ability to combine surrounding material into enormous fighting forms. His conviction is that true strength means standing alone above everyone else. That belief is tested by the alliances forming around him. Usopp’s refusal to abandon Luffy becomes especially important, even when he seems physically outmatched. Meanwhile, Marines and other forces converge on the festival, making survival more urgent than winning the advertised treasure.

sections.heading: An adventure without shortcuts
sections.text: Luffy and an improvised alliance break through Bullet’s defenses, with small acts of teamwork helping overcome an enemy obsessed with individual strength. The prize is revealed to offer a shortcut toward the final destination of the pirate journey. Luffy destroys that shortcut rather than let it decide his adventure for him. The survivors escape the battlefield, and the film closes on the idea that reaching a goal matters less if the freedom and uncertainty of the voyage have already been taken away.

title: Film Red

sections.heading: Uta’s concert
sections.text: The Straw Hats attend a concert by Uta, a singer whose voice has made her famous across the world. Luffy recognizes her from childhood and reveals their connection through Shanks. Her promise of a peaceful new era attracts listeners who are exhausted by violence and insecurity. The celebration becomes a crisis when her singing pulls audiences into Uta World, a reality shaped by her Devil Fruit power.

sections.heading: A perfect world with no way out
sections.text: Uta wants to keep people inside the world she controls so that pirates and suffering can no longer reach them. Her plan would take away their ability to choose their own lives. As the Straw Hats and other captives resist, the history of Elegia reveals how Uta’s memories and resentment were built around a tragedy she did not fully understand. Her use of wakefulness mushrooms worsens the danger, and the forbidden power of Tot Musica threatens both the dream space and the real world.

sections.heading: Two worlds, one battle
sections.text: Defeating Tot Musica requires coordinated attacks from inside Uta World and from the real world, where Shanks and his crew are fighting. Luffy’s group and Shanks’s group act together across that divide. After the entity is defeated, Uta chooses to sing again to free the trapped listeners, despite the cost to her exhausted body. The closing scenes strongly imply her death and show Shanks departing with his crew. The ending rejects a paradise imposed by force while treating Uta’s longing for peace as sincere and tragic.
